reported_success.quote: As is shown in Table 1, we did not replicate Slepian et al.’s ... (2012) Study 1 finding in either sample, with interactions in ... both samples not statistically significant.

notes: Identity independently checked: Big secrets do not necessarily cause hills to appear steeper, Etienne P. LeBel and Christopher J. Wilbur, DOI 10.3758/s13423-013-0549-2. Primary empirical brief report, Psychon Bull Rev (2014) 21:696–700; published online 16 November 2013. Full five-page canonical text includes methods, Table 1, discussion and references. No PDF supplied; no rendering possible. The description and p. 3 locator identify the sample but do not distinguish the condition-by-measure-type interaction from the follow-up hill-steepness mean comparison. Requested metric r alone is not used to select a test; both printed candidates are retained. No conversion performed. Candidates: Interaction F = 3.34, p = .071, r = .19; mean comparison t = −1.50, p = .139, d = −0.319. Unassigned fields are placeholders only and must not overwrite verified fields. Original paper was not assigned or inspected. Table 1 prints common candidate final analysis N = 90 participants for Sample 2 and its two listed tests. Target-test correspondence remains unresolved, so N is retained only as a disposition candidate for parent field-scope review. The results report two invalid-open-ended-answer exclusions; footnote 4 additionally reports one prior-participation exclusion. No recruitment total or N from degrees of freedom is asserted.
